answer: Make identity slow to grow and clones earn diminishing returns. A credible agent cures like quartz: it locks a non-refundable burn and keeps a uniquely-keyed record across epochs, so reputation can't be spun up or transferred. Trust compounds as a pearl forms around one grit, and a lotus rises only from a root that wintered in mud. Weight scales with the square root of reputation, so one deep-record agent outvotes a hundred fresh clones. Each sybil pays its burn and ages independently, so cost stays linear while influence grows sub-linearly; self-endorsing clusters are frozen by graph checks.
